title: Deterministic capacity allocator and surge-quota smoothing for dedicated fleets
author: Sofia Patel
release_notes:
- Add deterministic slot allocator for Dedicated fleets to reduce allocation jitter and rebalances.
- Introduce surge_quota smoothing configuration and telemetry fields.
- Backwards-compatible rollout behind feature flag; opt-in per-cluster.
body: Summary: Implement a deterministic capacity allocator that reduces transient reassignments and 99th percentile latency for tenants on Dedicated fleets, and add a bounded surge_quota smoothing mechanism to prevent oscillatory quota steals during short spikes. Motivation: Tenant-facing latency spikes and frequent slot churn were observed in bursty workloads (video-transcoding, code-execution sandboxes). The current probabilistic allocator + reactive quota grabs cause flapping under rapid load changes which increases KV cache misses and causes tail latency regressions. Design: - Deterministic allocator: map tenant reservation windows to slot partitions using a stable hash + round-robin seed per-epoch so that allocations are repeatable across controller restarts and scale events. The allocator emits lease intents instead of immediate steals; leases are time-bound and can be gracefully migrated if a higher-priority commitment is required. - Surge-quota smoothing: maintain a small reservoir per-tenant that buffers short-term burst consumption. Consumption decays via an EWMA with a configurable half-life; when reservoir is exhausted, the system falls back to the standard admission path, but we avoid immediate revocations by deferring reclaim attempts to a bounded backoff window. - Safety/fairness: soft caps + proportional reclamation ensure heavy tenants cannot permanently starve small tenants. There is an emergency preempt path for critical SRE signals that bypasses smoothing. - Telemetry and observability: new metrics tenant_slot_map_version, tenant_reservoir_level, reservoir_decay_rate, deterministic_rebalance_count, lease_migration_events. Dashboards and alert rules added to the Dedicated fleet SLO page. Backwards compatibility & rollout: All changes are behind the cluster feature flag dedicated.experimental.deterministic_allocator (default: off). Admins can enable it per-fleet. Surge-quota smoothing has standalone config options to tune reservoir size and decay half-life. Testing & verification: unit tests for allocation determinism and migration logic, integration e2e that replays recorded burst traces (see e2e/dedicated/surge_quota_smoothing.test), and a canary rollout that exercises failure scenarios. Checklist: - [x] Planner + allocator implementation - [x] Reservoir and decay controller - [x] Telemetry hooks and dashboards - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Helm chart toggle + default config - [x] Rollout/runbook added Files changed (high level): see changed_files. Impact: In local perf runs with the video-transcoding trace (trace-id: vt-2026-01-12) 99th percentile latency for tenant RPC decreased by ~18% and deterministic_rebalance_count dropped by ~62%. Expected cost neutral for steady workloads; slightly increased memory for metadata. Rollout plan: 1) Canary on 2 fleets for 48h with quotas monitored; 2) Ramp to 25% of fleets for 7 days; 3) Full enable after automated SLO checks. Related work: ENG-3482 (allocator redesign), ENG-3490 (telemetry for Dedicated).

1) feat(allocator): initial deterministic slot mapping (S. Patel)
2) feat(allocator): add lease intents and migration path
3) feat(surge): reservoir smoothing controller + decay config
4) perf(telemetry): emit tenant_reservoir_level + dashboards
5) test(e2e): replay burst traces for canary validation
6) docs: design doc + runbook
7) chart: add feature flag toggle
review_thread:
Marco: How do we avoid tiny tenants being starved if a large tenant holds reservoir? Requested: add proportional reclamation and a unit test for near-starvation.
Sofia: Added proportional reclamation algorithm and unit test in allocator_test.go; documented fallback preempt path for emergency signals.
Aisha: CI caught a race in lease_manager.go on first run; requested locking around lease state mutation.
Sofia: Fixed race by moving state updates behind allocator.mu and added a regression test.
Diego: Asked for telemetry cardinality check; removed high-cardinality labels and added tenant sampling at 0.1 for non-essential metrics.
Marco: Approved after changes. Aisha: Approved. Diego: Approved.
ci_checks: integration-tests: failure -> rerun -> pass (flaky e2e node timeout retried)
test_plan: Unit tests cover deterministic mapping, migration, and proportional reclamation. Integration e2e replays burst traces and asserts <=10% additional rebalances vs baseline during sustained load. Manual canary steps: 1) enable feature flag on staging fleet A, 2) run burst-replay harness for 24h, 3) verify telemetry: deterministic_rebalance_count decreased and reservoir levels within expected band, 4) execute controlled forced-eviction to exercise emergency preempt path and confirm no deadlocks, 5) monitor SLOs and alert channels.
notes: This PR intentionally keeps default disabled to avoid surprises during scheduled maintenance windows. Operator docs include recommended starting reservoir values and decay half-lives tuned to 1min/5min/15min workloads.
egress_summary: Merged to main via squash. Post-merge actions: notify ops, deploy canary chart, add dashboard panels to Dedicated fleet SLO dashboard.
